name: nRF24L01+
full_name: Nordic Semiconductor nRF24L01+ 2.4 GHz RF Transceiver (module)
description: Low-power 2.4 GHz ISM-band RF transceiver controlled over SPI, with an embedded Enhanced ShockBurst baseband protocol engine that handles packet assembly, auto-acknowledge and auto-retransmit in hardware. It supports data rates of 250 kbps, 1 Mbps and 2 Mbps across 125 selectable channels and up to 6 data pipes. The chip core runs at 1.9 to 3.6 V but its inputs are 5 V tolerant, so a 3.3 V supply with 5 V logic is workable. The common breakout exposes an 8-pin 2x4 header.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: ground (corner pin, usually marked on the board)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: 1.9-3.6 V supply; NOT 5 V tolerant on VCC, use 3.3 V

pins.name: CE
pins.description: chip enable; activates RX/TX (5 V tolerant logic)

pins.name: CSN
pins.description: SPI chip select, active low (5 V tolerant)

pins.name: MOSI
pins.description: SPI data in, master-out-slave-in (5 V tolerant)

pins.name: IRQ
pins.description: active-low interrupt (maskable: TX done / RX ready / max retransmit)

typical_application: Low-cost bidirectional wireless links between microcontrollers: remote sensors, RC, telemetry, and short-range home automation.
gotchas: VCC must be 3.3 V (1.9-3.6 V); 5 V on VCC destroys the chip even though the digital inputs are 5 V tolerant
the module is sensitive to supply noise; add a 10 uF (or larger) cap directly across VCC/GND at the module or it will drop packets/lock up
CE and CSN are separate: CE gates the radio (RX/TX) while CSN is the SPI chip-select - do not confuse them
the bare 2x4 header is easy to plug in rotated; pin 1 (GND) is marked on the PCB - orientation errors are the most common wiring fault
the '+' (nRF24L01+) variant adds the 250 kbps rate and is what is sold today; non-plus modules cannot interoperate at 250 kbps
PA+LNA long-range variants draw higher peak current and almost always need the external cap or a regulated 3.3 V rail
